hood_landmark.Bornheim: Berger Straße's café strip and market square
hood_landmark.Bockenheim: Bockenheimer Warte tower and its famous 'sinking tram' subway entrance

avoid.reason: Bahnhofsviertel (around the Hauptbahnhof) — open drug scene and red-light district; caution especially at night

hood_desc: Sachsenhausen sits just across the Main and pairs riverside museums with the cozy apple-wine taverns of Alt-Sachsenhausen, making it a lively pick for visitors who want nightlife, culture, and a walkable classic-Frankfurt feel.

Bornheim is a laid-back, family-friendly district built around the bustling Berger Strasse with its markets, cafes, and neighborhood pubs, suiting those who want an authentic residential vibe away from the tourist core.

Nordend is a leafy, upscale-but-relaxed residential area of handsome old apartment buildings, quiet streets, and independent cafes, ideal for professionals and families seeking a calm yet central base.
Westend is Frankfurt's elegant, affluent quarter of grand villas and green parks bordering the banking towers, best for those who want prestige, quiet, and proximity to the financial district.

Bockenheim is a diverse, youthful district anchored by the university, offering budget-friendly eats, ethnic groceries, and a bohemian energy that appeals to students and travelers seeking an unpretentious, multicultural scene.

water.note: Tap water is high quality and safe to drink straight from the tap.

transit.pay: No transit card needed - buy single tickets (about EUR 4) or day tickets (about EUR 7) from station machines or the RMVgo app; tickets are sold pre-validated, just board. One RMV ticket covers S-Bahn, U-Bahn, trams and buses, including the S-Bahn from the airport. Staying longer? The Deutschland-Ticket (EUR 58/month) covers local transit nationwide.
transit.hours: U-Bahn and S-Bahn run about 4:30am-1am; night buses and hourly weekend S-Bahn trains keep the city covered overnight Fri-Sat.

transit.m: S-Bahn S8/S9 to Hauptbahnhof, approx 11-15 min

food.desc: Translucent sour-milk cheese marinated in oil, vinegar and raw onions. The music is the onions, and the effect is legendary.

places.name: Atschel

food.desc: Cured pork loin chop gently poached and served on sauerkraut with mashed potato or bread and sharp mustard.

places.name: Lorsbacher Thal

food.name: Frankfurter Wuerstchen

places.name: Kleinmarkthalle
places.note: Covered market with butcher counters selling the real thing to eat standing up.

places.name: Apfelwein Wagner
places.note: Sausage plates with kraut and cider in the classic tavern setting.

food.name: Schnitzel Frankfurter Art
food.desc: Crisp pork schnitzel served, unusually, under a blanket of cold green herb sauce. A local pairing you rarely see elsewhere.

places.name: Zum Gemalten Haus
places.note: Generous portions and a proper Frankfurt tavern atmosphere; cash-friendly.

places.name: Fichtekraenzi
places.note: Reliable schnitzel and cider combination in one of the oldest houses on the strip.

places.name: Zur Buchscheer
places.note: Eat it in the tree-shaded garden in summer; book ahead at weekends.

food.name: Frankfurter Kranz
food.desc: Ring-shaped buttercream cake studded with brittle nut crocant, meant to echo a crown. A local coffee-house institution.

places.name: Cafe Hauptwache
places.note: Baroque guardhouse turned cafe in the city centre; cake and coffee on the terrace.

places.name: Kleinmarkthalle bakery stalls
places.note: Several counters sell slices to take away, alongside Bethmaennchen marzipan sweets.

places.name: Cafe Karin
places.note: Long-running cafe near the Goethe House, good for breakfast and cake alike.

food.name: Apfelwein (Ebbelwoi)
food.desc: Tart, still, low-alcohol apple wine poured from a blue-grey Bembel jug into ribbed Geripptes glasses. Order it sour, or mixed with water.

places.name: Zur Buchscheer
places.note: Presses its own cider on site; ask for Rauscher in autumn when it is young.

places.name: Fichtekraenzi
places.note: Bembel after Bembel at communal tables; the most sociable place to try it.

places.name: Apfelwein Solzer
places.note: Neighbourhood cider house with a mainly local crowd and fair prices.

food.name: German and craft beer
food.desc: Hessian pilsner and a lively local craft scene, plus Frankfurt's kiosk culture where you drink a bottle on the pavement.

places.name: Naiv
places.note: Craft beer bar in a half-timbered Altstadt house with a long rotating tap list.

places.name: Yok Yok
places.note: Legendary kiosk with hundreds of beers; drink them standing on the street outside.

places.name: Klaane Sachsehaeuser
places.note: If you want beer rather than cider in a traditional tavern, this is a safe bet.

landmarks: Römerberg
Frankfurt's historic town square lined with reconstructed half-timbered gabled houses, the picture-postcard heart of the Altstadt.
Römer (Old City Hall)
The distinctive triple-gabled medieval city hall on Römerberg square, Frankfurt's civic emblem for over 600 years.
Frankfurt Cathedral (Kaiserdom St. Bartholomäus)
A red-sandstone Gothic cathedral where Holy Roman Emperors were once elected and crowned, its tower offering city views.
Frankfurt Skyline / Main River waterfront
Nicknamed 'Mainhattan,' the cluster of skyscrapers along the Main River makes for Germany's most dramatic modern skyline photo.
Eiserner Steg
A wrought-iron pedestrian footbridge across the Main, dating to 1869, prized as the classic vantage point for skyline photos.
Main Tower
One of the few Frankfurt skyscrapers with a public observation deck, giving 360-degree views over the city and Taunus hills.
Alte Oper (Old Opera House)
A grand 19th-century Renaissance-style concert hall rebuilt after WWII, a favorite for its ornate facade and fountain-lined plaza.
Städel Museum
One of Germany's most important art museums, housing masterpieces from Dürer to Picasso along the scenic Museumsufer riverbank.
Goethe House (Goethehaus)
The restored birthplace and childhood home of writer Johann Wolfgang von Goethe, furnished as it was in the 18th century.
Palmengarten
A large botanical garden with historic glasshouses and tropical plant collections, a beloved green escape in the city center.

train.note: All of the above leave from Frankfurt Hauptbahnhof. Frankfurt has no direct night trains in the 2026 timetable - the Nightjet sleepers (e.g. Brussels-Vienna, Amsterdam-Zurich) call at nearby Mainz or Cologne instead, and the Paris night links were withdrawn in December 2025. Note that Frankfurt Flughafen Fernbahnhof at the airport is a separate long-distance station served by many ICE and TGV runs, so check which Frankfurt your ticket names.

intl.to: Paris, Amsterdam, Prague, Zurich & across Europe

bus.note: International coaches use the bus station on the south side of the Hauptbahnhof; many services also call at Frankfurt Airport, which is often the better boarding point. Tickets are bought online and the terminal has no full ticket office. Paris takes about 8h by coach, Amsterdam 6h and Prague 7h.

ferry.note: Frankfurt is far inland, so there are no ferries. Primus-Linie (https://www.primus-linie.de/) runs local sightseeing cruises on the River Main from the Eiserner Steg pier.

half.name: Heidelberg
half.blurb: Romantic university city crowned by a red ruined castle above the Neckar River.

half.name: Rüdesheim & the Rhine Valley
half.blurb: Vineyard slopes, castle-topped hills and wine taverns along the storied Rhine Gorge.

half.name: Rothenburg ob der Tauber
half.blurb: Perfectly preserved walled medieval town of half-timbered houses along the Romantic Road.

half.name: Würzburg
half.blurb: Baroque city known for its grand Residence palace and hillside vineyards above the Main.

half.name: Mainz
half.blurb: Riverside cathedral city, Gutenberg's home, with a lively old town and wine culture.

half.name: Eltz Castle
half.blurb: Fairy-tale medieval castle nestled in forested hills above a winding Moselle tributary.
